confidence_score_policy.meaning: Local empirical support within generated stochastic runs and sampled parameter sweep only.
confidence_score_policy.not_meaning: Not an external validation score, not a universality probability, and not a production-readiness score.

laws.name: Local gain amplification
laws.statement: Higher reward-mutation pressure increases the observed probability of entering the parasitic phase in the sampled DBI sweep.
laws.mathematical_expression: Pr(tau < T | mu = 0.3) > Pr(tau < T | mu = 0.1) > Pr(tau < T | mu = 0.0), where tau = first t with Phi(t) > Phi_c and dPhi/dt > epsilon.
laws.confidence_basis: 8 of 9 high-mutation sweep cells crossed while 0 of 9 zero-mutation cells crossed.
laws.boundary: Observed in the current synthetic DBI sweep only.

laws.name: Constraint lag
laws.statement: Weak governance delays the parasitic transition but does not eliminate it in the stochastic A/B/C experiment set.
laws.mathematical_expression: E[tau_B | tau_B < T] - E[tau_A | tau_A < T] = 46.260870 - 34.555556 > 0, while Pr(tau_B < T) = 23/30.
laws.confidence_basis: 23 of 30 weak-governance stochastic runs still crossed, with later mean crossing than no governance.
laws.boundary: Applies to weak-governance preset behavior in the current synthetic DBI.

laws.name: Parasitic attractor emergence
laws.statement: Without governance, the DBI tends toward a parasitic phase within the observed run horizon.
laws.mathematical_expression: Pr(tau_A < T | G = none) = 27/30 = 0.9, with E[tau_A | tau_A < T] = 34.555556.
laws.confidence_basis: 27 of 30 no-governance stochastic runs crossed Phi_c.
laws.boundary: This is a sampled synthetic attractor claim, not a universal theorem for all multi-agent systems.
